texts.firmware.20th_game: Another World 20th Anniversary Edition game folder
texts.firmware.20th_game.about: A zip of the game folder of the 20th Anniversary Edition (DAT, BMP or BGZ, WGZ, OGG, TXT). GOG's copy is inside its installer, which innoextract can open. Zips made by different people differ, so no particular file is required. You have to supply it, because this package includes none of the game's files. A file of your own can be used in its place, and the project then records its hash.
texts.firmware.3do_disc.about: The 3DO disc, as an image (.iso, with the data track's 2048-byte sectors) or as MAME's compressed image (.chd). The core reads it where it is, one block at a time, and copies none of it into the machine. You have to supply it, because this package includes none of the game's files. A file of your own can be used in its place, and the project then records its hash.
texts.firmware.amiga_en_disk1.about: The first disk of the English Amiga release (.adf, or a zip holding it, as TOSEC distributes them). It holds the program and bank01, 02, 06, 09, 0B, 0C and 0D. You have to supply it, because this package includes none of the game's files. A file of your own can be used in its place, and the project then records its hash.
texts.firmware.amiga_en_disk2.about: The second disk of the English Amiga release (.adf, or a zip holding it). It holds bank03, 04, 06, 07, 08, 09, 0A and 0C. You have to supply it, because this package includes none of the game's files. A file of your own can be used in its place, and the project then records its hash.
texts.firmware.amiga_fr_disk1.about: The first disk of the French Amiga release (.adf, or TOSEC's zip holding it). It is the uncracked disk, with the code-wheel copy protection. You have to supply it, because this package includes none of the game's files. A file of your own can be used in its place, and the project then records its hash.
texts.firmware.amiga_fr_disk2.about: The second disk of the French Amiga release (.adf, or TOSEC's zip holding it). You have to supply it, because this package includes none of the game's files. A file of your own can be used in its place, and the project then records its hash.
texts.firmware.atari_demo_disk: Another World Atari ST rolling demo disk
texts.firmware.atari_demo_disk.about: Cover disk 28 of the magazine ST Action (issue 44, December 1991), which holds the rolling demo AW.TOS. It can be the disk image (.st or .stx) or a zip of AW.TOS. You have to supply it, because this package includes none of the game's files. A file of your own can be used in its place, and the project then records its hash.
texts.firmware.atari_disk1.about: The first disk of the Atari ST release. It can be an .st, .msa or Pasti .stx image (copy protection included), or TOSEC's zip holding it. You have to supply it, because this package includes none of the game's files. A file of your own can be used in its place, and the project then records its hash.
texts.firmware.atari_disk2.about: The second disk of the Atari ST release (.st, .msa or .stx, or TOSEC's zip holding it). You have to supply it, because this package includes none of the game's files. A file of your own can be used in its place, and the project then records its hash.
texts.firmware.bank.about: The file BANK of the Windows 3.1 release. It holds the game's data. You have to supply it, because this package includes none of the game's files. A file of your own can be used in its place, and the project then records its hash.
texts.firmware.cm32l_control_rom.about: CM32L_CONTROL.ROM is not one of the game's files. It is the control ROM of the Roland CM-32L, version 1.02, used for the MT-32 Sound Effects setting. You have to supply it, because this package includes none of it. Another control ROM that Munt knows (the CM-32L's version 1.00, or an MT-32's) can be used in its place, and the project then records its hash. An MT-32 does not have the CM-32L's extra effect sounds, which some of rawgl's notes use.
texts.firmware.cm32l_pcm_rom.about: CM32L_PCM.ROM is not one of the game's files. It is the PCM ROM of the Roland CM-32L (1 MB), used for the MT-32 Sound Effects setting. You have to supply it, because this package includes none of it. Another PCM ROM that Munt knows can be used in its place, and the project then records its hash.
texts.firmware.dos_demo: Out of This World DOS demo
texts.firmware.dos_demo.about: Interplay's DOS demo from 1992, as the file it is distributed in (ootwdemo.zip, holding MEMLIST.BIN and five BANK files), or a zip of its files. You have to supply it, because this package includes none of the game's files. A file of your own can be used in its place, and the project then records its hash.
texts.firmware.dos_disk.about: The floppy disk image of the DOS release (.img or .ima), or a zip of the files on it (MEMLIST.BIN and the BANK files). The copy that was checked is GoodOldDays' Out of This World, one 1.2 MB disk. You have to supply it, because this package includes none of the game's files. A file of your own can be used in its place, and the project then records its hash.
texts.firmware.end2004_ogg.about: The file Music/End2004.ogg of the 15th Anniversary Edition, the music of the ending. You have to supply it, because this package includes none of the game's files. A file of your own can be used in its place, and the project then records its hash.
texts.firmware.intro2004_ogg.about: The file Music/Intro2004.ogg of the 15th Anniversary Edition, the music of the introduction. If your edition has Music/AW/Intro2004.wav in its place, use that file. You have to supply it, because this package includes none of the game's files. A file of your own can be used in its place, and the project then records its hash.
texts.firmware.lang_english_txt: Another World 15th Anniversary Edition English texts
texts.firmware.lang_english_txt.about: The file Menu/lang_English.Txt of the 15th Anniversary Edition. It holds the game's texts in English, used when the Language setting is English. You have to supply it, because this package includes none of the game's files. A file of your own can be used in its place, and the project then records its hash.
texts.firmware.lang_espanol_txt: Another World 15th Anniversary Edition Spanish texts
texts.firmware.lang_espanol_txt.about: The file Menu/lang_Español.txt of the 15th Anniversary Edition. It holds the game's texts in Spanish, used when the Language setting is Spanish. You have to supply it, because this package includes none of the game's files. A file of your own can be used in its place, and the project then records its hash.
texts.firmware.lang_francais_txt: Another World 15th Anniversary Edition French texts
texts.firmware.lang_francais_txt.about: The file Menu/lang_Français.Txt of the 15th Anniversary Edition. It holds the game's texts in French, used when the Language setting is French. You have to supply it, because this package includes none of the game's files. A file of your own can be used in its place, and the project then records its hash.
texts.firmware.pak01_pak.about: The file Data/Pak01.pak of the 15th Anniversary Edition. It holds the game. On the European CD it is inside the installer AnotherWorld_full.exe, which 7-Zip can open. You have to supply it, because this package includes none of the game's files. A file of your own can be used in its place, and the project then records its hash.
texts.firmware.soundfont_sf2.about: soundfont.sf2 is not one of the game's files. It is a General MIDI SoundFont (.sf2) of your choice, for example FluidR3 GM, GeneralUser GS or one sampled from a Roland Sound Canvas. It is used for the Windows 3.1 release's music (the SoundFont Music setting). No particular file is required. The project records the hash of the one you chose. Another SoundFont gives another sound, and the game stays the same.
texts.firmware.world_exe.about: The file WORLD.EXE of the Windows 3.1 release. It is the program, and it also holds pictures that rawgl reads. You have to supply it, because this package includes none of the game's files. A file of your own can be used in its place, and the project then records its hash.
texts.firmware.x_mid.about: The file X.MID of the Windows 3.1 release. It is music in General MIDI format, heard when the SoundFont Music setting is on. You have to supply it, because this package includes none of the game's files. A file of your own can be used in its place, and the project then records its hash.
texts.firmware.y_mid.about: The file Y.MID of the Windows 3.1 release. It is music in General MIDI format, heard when the SoundFont Music setting is on. You have to supply it, because this package includes none of the game's files. A file of your own can be used in its place, and the project then records its hash.
texts.property.alien_room: The room the alien is in
texts.property.engine_hero_action: The fire button, as the game reads it (VAR_HERO_ACTION)
texts.property.engine_hero_up_down: The joystick's up / down, as the game reads it (VAR_HERO_POS_UP_DOWN; Lester's swimming)
texts.property.engine_last_key: The letter typed on the password screen (VAR_LAST_KEYCHAR)
texts.property.engine_music_sync: What the music last told the script (VAR_MUSIC_SYNC)
texts.property.engine_pause_slices: The frame's length in fiftieths of a second (VAR_PAUSE_SLICES)
texts.property.engine_random_seed: The script's random number generator (the randomSeed setting starts it)
texts.property.game_next_part: The part the game goes to at its next frame (0: none)
texts.property.game_part: The part of the game being played
texts.property.game_screen: The screen the script last loaded
texts.property.lester_gun_load: The shot being charged (also the animation state)
texts.property.lester_has_gun: Nonzero once Lester has the gun
texts.property.machine_halted: The engine stopped on an error
texts.property.machine_time_ms: The machine's time since it started, in milliseconds
texts.property.world_timer: A countdown the level's script runs
texts.setting.difficulty.about: The difficulty of the 20th Anniversary Edition (rawgl's --difficulty option). The game's script reads it (variable 0xBF). The other releases have no difficulty setting.
texts.setting.language.about: The language rawgl uses (its --language option). It selects the game's texts. For the DOS, Amiga and Atari ST releases these are rawgl's own tables (French for 'fr', English otherwise). The anniversary editions and the Windows 3.1 release use their own text files. It also selects the DOS release's title screen, which says "Another World" in French and "Out of This World" otherwise. It changes what the game draws, so a movie records it.
texts.setting.mt32.about: Plays the DOS release's sound effects on a Roland CM-32L (rawgl's --mt32 option). rawgl has a note for 41 of the effects and sends those to the CM-32L's rhythm part, in place of the game's own samples. The CM-32L is emulated by Munt with the ROMs the project supplies as firmware (CM32L_CONTROL.ROM and CM32L_PCM.ROM). The music stays the game's own. It changes the sound only. The other releases ignore it.
texts.setting.randomseed.about: The starting value of the game script's random seed (script variable 0x3C). rawgl normally takes it from the clock, and the game's random numbers follow from it. The 20th Anniversary Edition also uses it to choose between sound variants. A movie records the number it ran with.
texts.setting.release.about: Which release of Another World this project plays (it is the System in Chimera). "dos" is Another World (DOS). "amiga" is Another World (Amiga, English). "amigafr" is Another World (Amiga, French). "atari" is Another World (Atari ST). "win31" is Out of This World (Windows 3.1). "3do" is Out of This World (3DO). "15th" is the 15th Anniversary Edition. "20th" is the 20th Anniversary Edition. "dosdemo" is the Out of This World DOS demo. "stdemo" is the Atari ST rolling demo. The release decides which of the game's files the project needs (as firmware) and which settings apply. rawgl plays the files as it finds them.
texts.setting.remasteredaudio.about: Chooses between the remastered sounds and music of the anniversary editions (rawgl's default, --audio=remastered) and the original ones. The originals are the 15th's Data files and Music/AW, and the 20th's game/WGZ/original and game/OGG/original. The 20th's script also reads this choice (variable 0xDE). The other releases have only one set of sounds.
texts.setting.soundfont.about: Plays the Windows 3.1 release's music. The music is two General MIDI files, which the original played on the PC's MIDI synthesizer. Here TinySoundFont plays them with a General MIDI SoundFont that the project supplies as firmware (soundfont.sf2, any .sf2 file of your choice, and the project records which one). With this off the music is silent, as in rawgl without a MIDI synthesizer. It changes the sound only. The game and its timing are the same either way. The other releases ignore it.
